s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and shortness of breath with a history of arrhythmia
salient_findings: Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform
Incomplete right bundle branch block morphology on ECG
key_facts: 20-year history of palpitations and shortness of breath
Episodes were previously controlled with verapamil
Sustained symptoms recurred 6 months before presentation
Not responding to amiodarone therapy
Heart rate: 122 beats per minute
Blood pressure: 135/85 mm Hg
ECG shows regular tachycardia at 130 beats per minute
QRS duration of 118 milliseconds
Left-axis deviation
P-wave morphology shows negative deflection in leads II and aVF
24-hour Holter monitor showed sustained tachycardia throughout monitoring period
Echocardiogram results within normal limits

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Regular tachycardia with P-wave morphology showing negative deflection in leads II and aVF, consistent with AVNRT

shortlist.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Sustained tachycardia with 3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations, possible orthodromic AVRT

shortlist.label: Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Regular tachycardia with left-axis deviation, possible atrial flutter

shortlist.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia with Aberrancy

shortlist.label: Focal Atrial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Sustained tachycardia with P-wave morphology showing negative deflection in leads II and aVF, possible focal atrial tachycardia

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows regular tachycardia with a 3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations, and P-wave morphology with negative deflection in leads II and aVF, which is consistent with Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia. The patient's history of palpitations and shortness of breath, previously controlled with verapamil, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a wider QRS complex due to the presence of an accessory pathway, which is not seen in this patient's ECG.

rejected.label: Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: Atrial Flutter typically presents with a sawtooth pattern on the ECG, which is not present in this patient's ECG.

rejected.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia with Aberrancy
rejected.why: This condition would likely present with a more irregular rhythm and a wider QRS complex, which is not seen in this patient's ECG.

rejected.label: Focal Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a more irregular rhythm and P-wave morphology that is different from what is seen in this patient's ECG.
